# Testing & Quality Assurance Rules

These rules apply to all test files and quality assurance activities in
**{{projectName}}**.

## Test Pyramid

| Layer | Tool | Location | Notes |
| ----- | ---- | -------- | ----- |
{{#if testingUnit}}| Unit | {{testingUnit}} | `**/*.test.*` / `**/*.spec.*` | Fast, isolated, no I/O |
{{/if}}{{#if testingIntegration}}| Integration | {{testingIntegration}} | `tests/integration/` | Module interactions |
{{/if}}{{#if testingE2e}}| E2E | {{testingE2e}} | `tests/e2e/` / `e2e/` | Full user workflows |
{{/if}}

## Coverage

{{#if testingCoverage}}- Minimum coverage target: **{{testingCoverage}}%** (line, branch, and function).{{/if}}

- No pull request may decrease overall coverage from the current baseline.
- Enforce the threshold in CI — fail the build when coverage drops below the minimum.
- Use coverage reports to identify untested branches, not just lines.

## Naming Conventions

- Test files must mirror the source structure: `src/foo/bar.ts` → `src/foo/bar.test.ts`.
- Describe blocks: name of the unit under test (class, function, module).
- It/test blocks: `should <verb> <expected outcome>` in plain English.
- Name test helpers with the `make*` or `build*` prefix (e.g. `makeUser()`).

## Test Structure (AAA)

Every test must follow **Arrange → Act → Assert**:

```
describe('PaymentService', () => {
  it('should reject a payment when the card is expired', async () => {
    // Arrange
    const card = makeCard({ expired: true });

    // Act
    const result = await paymentService.charge(card, 100);

    // Assert
    expect(result.success).toBe(false);
    expect(result.errorCode).toBe('CARD_EXPIRED');
  });
});
```

## Mocking & Isolation

- Mock at system boundaries (HTTP clients, databases, queues) — not internal
  module details.
- Prefer dependency injection to make units testable without patching internals.
- Never mock the unit under test itself.
- Document why each mock is necessary with a short comment.

## Forbidden Patterns

- No `setTimeout` / `Thread.Sleep` / `time.sleep` in tests — use deterministic
  waits (`waitFor`, `waitUntil`, polling helpers).
- No permanently skipped tests (`it.skip`, `@Ignore`, `[Fact(Skip=...)]`).
  Temporary skips must reference a tracking issue and be resolved within
  one sprint.
- No shared mutable state between tests — each test must be independent and
  runnable in any order.

## Integration Tests

- Use per-test database transactions with rollback, or fresh containers
  (Testcontainers / Docker Compose) per test suite.
- Integration tests must clean up all side-effects (files, queues, database rows).
- Keep integration tests in a separate suite from unit tests so CI can run
  them independently.

{{#if testingE2e}}

## End-to-End Tests

- Tag smoke tests (`@smoke`) so the critical path subset runs on every deploy.
- Quarantine flaky tests immediately — move to a separate suite and fix within
  two sprints.
- Use explicit waits and retry strategies; never use arbitrary sleep.
- Scope E2E tests to user-visible behaviour, not internal implementation.
  {{/if}}

## Quality Gates

Before merging any pull request:

- [ ] All unit tests pass locally
      {{#if testingCoverage}}- [ ] Coverage meets or exceeds the {{testingCoverage}}% threshold{{/if}}{{#unless testingCoverage}}- [ ] Coverage target is met{{/unless}}
- [ ] No permanently skipped tests added
- [ ] No flaky tests introduced
- [ ] CI passes (lint + type-check + tests)
